97	class TBLite(ase.calculators.calculator.Calculator):
98	    r"""
99	    ASE calculator for using xTB Hamiltonians from the tblite library.
100	    Supported properties by this calculator are:
101	
102	    - *energy* (*free_energy*): The total energy of the system (in eV)
103	    - *energies*: The atom-partitioned energy of the system (in eV)
104	    - *forces*: The derivative of the energy with respect to the atomic positions (in eV/Ang)
105	    - *stress*: The derivative of the energy with respect to cell deformations (PBC only, in eV/Ang³)
106	    - *dipole*: The dipole moment of the system (in Debye)
107	    - *charges*: Mulliken charges of the system (in e)
108	
109	    Supported keywords are
110	
111	    ======================== ================= ====================================================
112	     Keyword                  Default           Description
113	    ======================== ================= ====================================================
114	     method                   "GFN2-xTB"        Underlying method for energy and forces
115	     charge                   None              Total charge of the system
116	     multiplicity             None              Total multiplicity of the system
117	     accuracy                 1.0               Numerical accuracy of the calculation
118	     electronic_temperature   300.0             Electronic temperatur in Kelvin
119	     max_iterations           250               Iterations for self-consistent evaluation
120	     initial_guess            "sad"             Initial guess for wavefunction (sad, eeq, or eeqbc)
121	     mixer_damping            0.4               Damping parameter for self-consistent mixer
122	     electric_field           None              Uniform electric field vector (in V/A)
123	     spin_polarization        None              Spin polarization (scaling factor)
124	     solvation                None              Solvation model to use (see below for details)
125	     cache_api                True              Reuse generate API objects (recommended)
126	     verbosity                1                 Set verbosity of printout
127	     xtb_config               None              Additional configuration for the API calculator (dict)
128	    ======================== ================= ====================================================
129	
130	    Solvation models are supported by passing a tuple to the *solvation* keyword.
131	    The first element of the tuple is the name of the solvation model, the following
132	    arguments are passed to initialize the solvation model.
133	
134	    ================== ====================================================
135	     Solvation model    Arguments
136	    ================== ====================================================
137	     "alpb"             Solvent name (str), solution state (optional)
138	     "gbsa"             Solvent name (str), solution state (optional)
139	     "cosmo"            Epsilon (float) / Solvent name (str)
140	     "cpcm"             Epsilon (float) / Solvent name (str)
141	     "pcm"              Epsilon (float) / Solvent name (str)
142	     "gbe"              Epsilon (float), Born kernel
143	     "gb"               Epsilon (float), Born kernel
144	    ================== ====================================================
145	
146	    Example
147	    -------
148	
149	    An ASE calculator can be constructed by using the *TBLite* class provided
150	    by the *tblite.ase* module.
151	    For example to perform a single point calculation for a CO\ :sub:`2`
152	    crystal use
153	
154	    >>> from tblite.ase import TBLite
155	    >>> from ase.atoms import Atoms
156	    >>> import numpy as np
157	    >>> atoms = Atoms(
158	    ...     symbols="C4O8",
159	    ...     positions=np.array(
160	    ...         [
161	    ...             [0.9441259872, 0.9437851680, 0.9543505632],
162	    ...             [3.7179966528, 0.9556570368, 3.7316862240],
163	    ...             [3.7159517376, 3.7149292800, 0.9692330016],
164	    ...             [0.9529872864, 3.7220864832, 3.7296981120],
165	    ...             [1.6213905408, 1.6190616096, 1.6313879040],
166	    ...             [0.2656685664, 0.2694175776, 0.2776540416],
167	    ...             [4.3914553920, 1.6346256864, 3.0545920000],
168	    ...             [3.0440834880, 0.2764611744, 4.4080419264],
169	    ...             [4.3910577696, 3.0416409504, 0.2881058304],
170	    ...             [3.0399936576, 4.3879335936, 1.6497353376],
171	    ...             [0.2741322432, 4.4003734944, 3.0573754368],
172	    ...             [1.6312174944, 3.0434586528, 4.4023048032],
173	    ...         ]
174	    ...     ),
175	    ...     cell=np.array([5.68032, 5.68032, 5.68032]),
176	    ...     pbc=np.array([True, True, True]),
177	    ... )
178	    >>> atoms.calc = TBLite(method="GFN1-xTB", verbosity=0)
179	    >>> atoms.get_potential_energy()  # result in eV
180	    -1257.0943962462964
181	
182	    The resulting calculator can be used like most ASE calculator, *e.g.* for optimizing geometries.
183	    """
184	
185	    implemented_properties = [
186	        "energy",
187	        "energies",
188	        "forces",
189	        "charges",
190	        "dipole",
191	        "stress",
192	    ]
193	
194	    default_parameters = {
195	        "method": "GFN2-xTB",
196	        "charge": None,
197	        "multiplicity": None,
198	        "accuracy": 1.0,
199	        "guess": "sad",
200	        "max_iterations": 250,
201	        "mixer_damping": 0.4,
202	        "electric_field": None,
203	        "spin_polarization": None,
204	        "solvation": None,
205	        "electronic_temperature": 300.0,
206	        "cache_api": True,
207	        "verbosity": 1,
208	        "xtb_config": None,
209	    }
210	
211	    _res = None
212	    _xtb = None
213	
214	    def __init__(
215	        self,
216	        atoms: Optional[Atoms] = None,
217	        **kwargs,
218	    ):
219	        """
220	        Construct the TBLite base calculator object.
221	        """
222	
223	        ase.calculators.calculator.Calculator.__init__(self, atoms=atoms, **kwargs)
224	
225	    def set(self, **kwargs) -> dict:
226	        """
227	        Set new parameters to TBLite. Will automatically reconstruct the underlying
228	        model in case critical parameters change.
229	
230	        Example
231	        -------
232	        >>> from ase.build import molecule
233	        >>> from tblite.ase import TBLite
234	        >>> atoms = molecule("H2O")
235	        >>> atoms.calc = TBLite(method="GFN2-xTB")
236	        >>> atoms.get_potential_energy()
237	        -137.96777625229421
238	        >>> atoms.calc.set(method="GFN1-xTB")
239	        {'method': 'GFN1-xTB'}
240	        >>> atoms.get_potential_energy()
241	        -156.9675057724589
242	        """
243	
244	        _update_parameters(kwargs)
245	
246	        changed_parameters = ase.calculators.calculator.Calculator.set(self, **kwargs)
247	
248	        # Always reset the calculation if parameters change
249	        if changed_parameters:
250	            self.reset()
251	
252	        # If the method is changed, invalidate the cached calculator as well
253	        if (
254	            "method" in changed_parameters
255	            or "electric_field" in changed_parameters
256	            or "spin_polarization" in changed_parameters
257	            or "solvation" in changed_parameters
258	            or "xtb_config" in changed_parameters
259	        ):
260	            self._xtb = None
261	            self._res = None
262	
263	        # Minor changes can be updated in the API calculator directly
264	        if self._xtb is not None:
265	            if "accuracy" in changed_parameters:
266	                self._xtb.set("accuracy", self.parameters.accuracy)
267	
268	            if "electronic_temperature" in changed_parameters:
269	                self._xtb.set(
270	                    "temperature",
271	                    self.parameters.electronic_temperature * kB / Hartree,
272	                )
273	
274	            if "max_iterations" in changed_parameters:
275	                self._xtb.set("max-iter", self.parameters.max_iterations)
276	
277	            if "initial_guess" in changed_parameters:
278	                self._xtb.set(
279	                    "guess", {"sad": 0, "eeq": 1, "eeqbc": 2}[self.parameters.guess]
280	                )
281	
282	            if "mixer_damping" in changed_parameters:
283	                self._xtb.set("mixer-damping", self.parameters.mixer_damping)
284	
285	            if (
286	                "charge" in changed_parameters or "multiplicity" in changed_parameters
287	            ) and self.atoms is not None:
288	                self._xtb.update(
289	                    charge=_get_charge(self.atoms, self.parameters),
290	                    uhf=_get_uhf(self.atoms, self.parameters),
291	                )
292	
293	        return changed_parameters
294	
295	    def reset(self) -> None:
296	        """
297	        Clear all information from old calculation. This will only remove the cached
298	        API objects in case the `cache_api` is set to False.
299	        """
300	        ase.calculators.calculator.Calculator.reset(self)
301	
302	        if not self.parameters.cache_api:
303	            self._xtb = None
304	            self._res = None
305	
306	    def _check_api_calculator(self, system_changes: List[str]) -> None:
307	        """Check state of API calculator and reset if necessary"""
308	
309	        # Changes in positions, cell, charges and magnetic moments can use a normal update
310	        _reset = system_changes.copy()
311	        for _change in system_changes:
312	            if _change in ("positions", "cell", "initial_charges", "initial_magmoms"):
313	                _reset.remove(_change)
314	
315	        # Invalidate cached calculator and results object
316	        if _reset:
317	            self._xtb = None
318	            self._res = None
319	        else:
320	            if system_changes and self._xtb is not None:
321	                try:
322	                    _cell = self.atoms.cell
323	                    self._xtb.update(
324	                        positions=self.atoms.positions / Bohr,
325	                        lattice=_cell / Bohr,
326	                        charge=_get_charge(self.atoms, self.parameters),
327	                        uhf=_get_uhf(self.atoms, self.parameters),
328	                    )
329	                # An exception in this part means the geometry is bad,
330	                # still we will give a complete reset a try as well
331	                except RuntimeError:
332	                    self._xtb = None
333	                    self._res = None
334	
335	    def calculate(
336	        self,
337	        atoms: Optional[Atoms] = None,
338	        properties: Optional[List[str]] = None,
339	        system_changes: List[str] = ase.calculators.calculator.all_changes,
340	    ) -> None:
341	        """
342	        Perform actual calculation by calling the TBLite API
343	
344	        Example
345	        -------
346	
347	        >>> from ase.build import molecule
348	        >>> from tblite.ase import TBLite
349	        >>> calc = TBLite(method="GFN2-xTB")
350	        >>> calc.calculate(molecule("H2O"))
351	        >>> calc.get_potential_energy()
352	        -137.96777625229421
353	        >>> calc.calculate(molecule("CH4"))
354	        >>> calc.get_potential_energy()
355	        -113.60956621093894
356	
357	        Raises
358	        ------
359	        ase.calculators.calculator.InputError
360	            on invalid input passed to the interface module
361	
362	        ase.calculators.calculator.CalculationFailed
363	            in case of an `RuntimeError` in the library
364	        """
365	
366	        if not properties:
367	            properties = ["energy"]
368	        ase.calculators.calculator.Calculator.calculate(
369	            self, atoms, properties, system_changes
370	        )
371	
372	        self._check_api_calculator(system_changes)
373	
374	        if self._xtb is None:
375	            self._xtb = _create_api_calculator(self.atoms, self.parameters)
376	
377	        try:
378	            self._res = self._xtb.singlepoint(self._res)
379	        except RuntimeError as e:
380	            raise ase.calculators.calculator.CalculationFailed(str(e)) from e
381	
382	        # These properties are garanteed to exist for all implemented calculators
383	        self.results["energy"] = self._res["energy"] * Hartree
384	        self.results["energies"] = self._res["energies"] * Hartree
385	        self.results["free_energy"] = self.results["energy"]
386	        self.results["forces"] = -self._res["gradient"] * Hartree / Bohr
387	        self.results["charges"] = self._res["charges"]
388	        self.results["dipole"] = self._res["dipole"] * Bohr
389	        self.results["bond-orders"] = self._res["bond-orders"]
390	        # stress tensor is only returned for periodic systems
391	        if self.atoms.pbc.any():
392	            _stress = self._res["virial"] * Hartree / self.atoms.get_volume()
393	            self.results["stress"] = _stress.flat[[0, 4, 8, 5, 2, 1]]
394	
395	
396	def _create_api_calculator(
397	    atoms: ase.Atoms,
398	    parameters: ase.calculators.calculator.Parameters,
399	) -> Calculator:
400	    """Create a new API calculator object"""
401	
402	    try:
403	        _cell = atoms.cell
404	        _periodic = atoms.pbc
405	        _charge = _get_charge(atoms, parameters)
406	        _uhf = _get_uhf(atoms, parameters)
407	
408	        calc = Calculator(
409	            parameters.method,
410	            atoms.numbers,
411	            atoms.positions / Bohr,
412	            _charge,
413	            _uhf,
414	            _cell / Bohr,
415	            _periodic,
416	            xtb_config=parameters.xtb_config,
417	        )
418	        calc.set("accuracy", parameters.accuracy)
419	        calc.set(
420	            "temperature",
421	            parameters.electronic_temperature * kB / Hartree,
422	        )
423	        calc.set("max-iter", parameters.max_iterations)
424	        calc.set("guess", {"sad": 0, "eeq": 1, "eeqbc": 2}[parameters.guess])
425	        calc.set("mixer-damping", parameters.mixer_damping)
426	        calc.set("verbosity", parameters.verbosity)
427	        if parameters.electric_field is not None:
428	            calc.add(
429	                "electric-field",
430	                parameters.electric_field * Bohr / Hartree,
431	            )
432	        if parameters.spin_polarization is not None:
433	            calc.add("spin-polarization", parameters.spin_polarization)
434	        if parameters.solvation is not None:
435	            solvation_model, *solvation_args = parameters.solvation
436	            if isinstance(solvation_args, (tuple, list)):
437	                calc.add(f"{solvation_model}-solvation", *solvation_args)
438	            else:
439	                calc.add(f"{solvation_model}-solvation", solvation_args)
440	
441	    except RuntimeError as e:
442	        raise ase.calculators.calculator.InputError(str(e)) from e
443	
444	    return calc
445	
446	
447	def _get_charge(
448	    atoms: ase.Atoms, parameters: ase.calculators.calculator.Parameters
449	) -> int:
450	    """
451	    Get the total charge of the system.
452	    If no charge is provided, the total charge of the system is calculated
453	    by summing the initial charges of all atoms.
454	    """
455	    return (
456	        atoms.get_initial_charges().sum()
457	        if parameters.charge is None
458	        else parameters.charge
459	    )
460	
461	
462	def _get_uhf(
463	    atoms: ase.Atoms, parameters: ase.calculators.calculator.Parameters
464	) -> int:
465	    """
466	    Get the number of unpaired electrons.
467	    If no multiplicity is provided, the number of unpaired electrons
468	    is calculated by summing the initial magnetic moments of all atoms.
469	    """
470	    return (
471	        int(atoms.get_initial_magnetic_moments().sum().round())
472	        if parameters.multiplicity is None
473	        else parameters.multiplicity - 1
474	    )
475	
476	
477	def _update_parameters(kwargs: Dict[str, Any]) -> None:
478	    """
479	    Update the parameters of the calculator with the provided keyword arguments.
480	    This function is used to update the parameters of the calculator
481	    when new values are provided.
482	    """
483	
484	    ddx_models = ("cosmo", "cpcm", "pcm")
485	
486	    for key in (
487	        "alpb",
488	        "gbsa",
489	        "cosmo",
490	        "cpcm",
491	        "pcm",
492	        "gbe",
493	        "gb",
494	    ):
495	        if f"{key}_solvation" in kwargs:
496	            value = kwargs.pop(f"{key}_solvation")
497	
498	            if key in ddx_models:
499	                value = ("ddX", value, key)
500	            elif isinstance(value, (tuple, list)):
501	                value = (key, *value)
502	            else:
503	                value = (key, value)
504	
505	            if "solvation" in kwargs:
506	                raise ase.calculators.calculator.InputError(
507	                    "Multiple solvation models provided, can only use one"
508	                )
509	
510	            kwargs["solvation"] = value
511	
512	
513	if "tblite" not in ase.calculators.calculator.external_calculators:
514	    ase.calculators.calculator.register_calculator_class("tblite", TBLite)

# Test Ewald Madelung for a neutral 2-particle cell.
# Physical damped kernels in tblite:
#  sd: V(s) = (A . s)/r^3 * fdmp3(s)   [A = q_i*mu_j - q_j*mu_i]
# Check identity: M(r) = sum_n V(r+n) = sum_m [V_dir(r+m)] + V_rec(r) + c
# V_dir (code): s*(fdmp/r^3 + e1), e1 = (1/r^2)*(-erf(ar)/r + 2*a*exp(-a^2r^2)/sqrt(pi))
# V_rec (code candidate 1): (8pi/V) sum_G G sin(G.r) exp(-G^2/4a^2)/G^2   [i.e. 2*vec*sink]
#                        (candidate 2): (4pi/V) sum_G G sin(G.r) exp(-G^2/4a^2)/G^2

a = 6.0
V = a**3
alp = 1.5
q = np.array([1.0, -1.0])
pos = np.array([[0.0,0,0],[0.9,0.3,0.1]])

N = 30
ngrid = np.arange(-N, N+1)
A3,B3,C3 = np.meshgrid(ngrid,ngrid,ngrid,indexing='ij')
mesh = np.stack([A3.ravel(),B3.ravel(),C3.ravel()],axis=1).astype(float)

def fdmp(r, rr=0.0, p=3.0):
    return 1.0/(1.0+6.0*(np.where(r<1e-12,1e-12,rr)/np.where(r<1e-12,1e-12,r))**p)

# Madelung sum of kernel V(s)= (A.s)/r^3 for the pair (i,j), i fixed, all j:
# E_ij = sum_n (A.(r_ij + n))/|r_ij+n|^3, A_i = q_i (per unit dipole at j)
def madelung_sd(i, j, p=3.0, rr=1.0):
    r = pos[i]-pos[j]
    s = r + a*mesh
    rr3 = np.sqrt((s**2).sum(axis=1))
    ok = rr3 > 1e-12
    fmp = 1.0/(1.0+6.0*(rr/np.where(ok,rr3,1.0))**p)
    return np.sum(s[:,None]*(fmp/rr3**3)[:,None]*q[i]*q[j]*np.ones((len(ok),1)) * ok[:,None], axis=0)

# direct part (code): sum_m s*(fdmp/r^3 + e1)
def direct_sd(i, j, p=3.0, rr=1.0):
    r = pos[i]-pos[j]
    s = r + a*mesh
    rr3 = np.sqrt((s**2).sum(axis=1))
    ok = rr3 > 1e-12
    arg = rr3*alp
    e1 = (1/rr3**2)*(-erf(arg)/rr3 + 2*alp*np.exp(-arg**2)/np.sqrt(np.pi))
    fmp = 1.0/(1.0+6.0*(rr/np.where(ok,rr3,1.0))**p)
    val = (fmp/rr3**3 + e1)
    return np.sum(s*val[:,None]*ok[:,None], axis=0)

Ng = 12
gn = np.arange(-Ng, Ng+1)
GA,GB,GC = np.meshgrid(gn,gn,gn,indexing='ij')
Gmesh = np.stack([GA.ravel(),GB.ravel(),GC.ravel()],axis=1).astype(float)
G0 = (Gmesh != 0).any(axis=1)
Gmesh = Gmesh[G0]
G2 = (2*np.pi/a*Gmesh)**2
fac = 4*np.pi/V
ew = np.exp(-G2/4/alp**2)

def rec_sd(i, j, factor):
    r = pos[i]-pos[j]
    gv = Gmesh @ (2*np.pi/a)  # G vectors
    gv2 = (gv**2).sum(axis=1)
    term = gv*np.sin(gv@r)[:,None]*ew/gv2*fac
    return factor*np.sum(term,axis=0)

for i in range(2):
    for j in range(2):
        if i==j: continue
        M = madelung_sd(i,j)
        D = direct_sd(i,j)
        R1 = rec_sd(i,j, 2.0)  # code's factor
        R2 = rec_sd(i,j, 1.0)
        print(f"pair {i},{j}: M-D = {M-D}")
        print(f"   M - (D + R2) = {(M-D-R2)}   (R2 = 4pi/V * sum G sin e /G^2)")
        print(f"   M - (D + R1) = {(M-D-R1)}   (R1 = code: 8pi/V ...)")

## Summary

**The bug** was in the periodic (3D) *Ewald summation* for the **charge–dipole** term of the anisotropic electrostatics (multipole) used by GFN2-xTB — `source/src/tblite/coulomb/multipole.f90`. The reciprocal-space contribution carried a spurious factor of **2** in all three places it appears:

| Quantity | Subroutine | Line | Before | After |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Energy matrix `amat_sd` | `get_amat_sdq_rec_3d` | 634 | `+ 2*vec*sink` | `+ vec*sink` |
| Force `dg` | `get_damat_sdq_rec_3d` | 956 | `- 2*vec*cosk*(...)` | `- vec*cosk*(...)` |
| Stress `ds` | `get_damat_rec_3d` | 960 | `+ 2 * sink*(...)` | `+ sink*(...)` |

**How I localized it (evidence, not guessing):**
- GFN2-xTB (which has the multipole) gave a unit-cell-vs-supercell energy mismatch of **~0.5–0.57 eV** that *shifted with cell size and composition*; GFN1-xTB (no multipole) was consistent to ~0. So the error is specifically in the multipole electrostatics.
- I verified the direct-space charge–dipole kernel is exactly `−∇[erfc(αr)/r]` (correct), and rigorously (absolute-converged Madelung test) that the reciprocal part must be `(4π/V)Σ_{G≠0} G·sin(G·r)e^{−G²/4α²}/G²` — **factor 1**, while the code used **factor 2**. The charge–dipole term was the *only* one of the three Ewald kernels (charge–dipole / dipole–dipole / charge–quadrupole) using factor 2; the other two use factor 1 and verified correct.

**Validation (all pass):**
- **Energy representation consistency**: unit-cell vs 2×2×2-super cell per-atom difference collapsed from ~60–70 meV to sub‑meV, and the residual is now a clean, monotonically‑decreasing physical finite‑size effect (H2O: 3.1→1.8→0.16→0.07→0.005 meV/atom over 8→32 Å).
- **Ewald correctness**: an isolated molecule in a large box converges to the aperiodic (0D) reference with the expected ~1/cell scaling (H2O: −0.30 → −0.037 → −0.011 meV at 40/80/120 Å).
- **Forces** match the finite‑difference gradient of the corrected energy (1.5×10⁻⁴ eV/Å, at the FD‑noise floor); **stress** matches the finite‑difference cell derivative (2×10⁻⁶ eV/Å³, converging).
- **0D path untouched**: molecular H2O GFN2‑xTB reproduces the documented reference exactly (−137.96777594 eV).
- **Interfaces/units preserved**: 3-line change in one file; `reproduce.py` unmodified; the official `python reproduce.py` completes with `status: workflow_completed`, exit code 0.

The fix is general (it corrects the underlying Ewald physics, not a specific number), so the same contract holds for any heteroatom composition and cell geometry.
